name: Don't Scroll Before Zero
why_it_works: A visible countdown turns watching into a small game with a clear finish line. The brain hates leaving something unfinished, so a timer on screen keeps people until zero, and watch-through is what the algorithm rewards.

hook.pattern: Put a ticking timer on screen and tell the viewer the good part happens at zero.
examples: Ten seconds. The last one is worth it.

variables.name: creation
variables.description: What is being made or revealed

variables.name: final_detail
variables.description: The detail that appears at zero
variables.example: a perfect rosetta in one pour

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer can do next
variables.example: show this video for $1 off today

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 close-up of the starting point of the {{creation}} on a {{brand}} counter, moody side light, empty space at top for a large timer overlay
Fast close-up of hands making the {{creation}}, steady overhead angle, warm practical light, vertical 9:16, motion slightly sped up
The {{creation}} a moment before finishing, the key detail just out of frame, shallow depth of field, warm light, vertical 9:16
Slow push-in on the finished {{creation}} showing {{final_detail}}, warm light, steam or texture visible, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: Burn the countdown into the frame in big numbers, and make the timer reach zero exactly as the reveal lands. Cut the last frame so it loops cleanly back to the first, which drives replays.

do_not: Let the reveal happen before zero; it breaks the promise
Use a reveal that is not visually obvious on a phone screen
Pad the timer past 10 seconds; long countdowns feel like a trick
